clean_source_blocks.text: Allegra Spender (left) and Zali Steggall say their new party will offer 'reason over rage' Two independent Australian MPs have banded together to launch a new centrist political party which they say is a response to an increasingly divisive landscape. The Community Strong Australia party - launched in Canberra on Thursday - will offer "unity over division and reason over rage", will have no leader and will allow members to vote freely, rather than along party lines. Its two members - Sydney MPs Zali Steggall and Allegra Spender - are from a group of independent MPs known as "teals" who share socially liberal values and want greater climate action. The party will offer an "alternate political force" to the current two-party system in Australia, the pair said.

Zali Steggall and Allegra Spender say Community Strong Australia will offer citizens 'reason over rage'. Karl Stefanovic has helmed a popular breakfast TV show for the better part of two decades. The group says that it is unlawful for Australia to continue approving fossil fuel exports without protecting its citizens. Police seized 2.7 tonnes of cocaine worth an estimated A$816m after searching a property in western Sydney. Ahmed al Ahmed tackled one of the gunmen who killed 15 people at a Jewish event in December. Leah Stewart, 34, had one of her arms amputated after she was bitten while swimming at Coogee Beach. Researchers say their hunting method - which allows them to prey on dangerous ants - is unprecedented. Nestory Irankunda was born as a refugee in Tanzania before becoming Australian record breaker with goal in victory over Turkey.
Zali Steggall and Allegra Spender say Community Strong Australia will offer citizens 'reason over rage'.

The party will focus on issues including housing affordability, cost of living, climate change, childcare, education, healthcare and social cohesion, according to Steggall, the member for Warringah. She and Spender have distanced the new party from the Climate 200 movement and its major donors, including Scott Farquhar and Mike Cannon-Brooks, stating on Thursday they would not be involved.

Allegra Spender (left) and Zali Steggall say their new party will offer 'reason over rage'

Two independent Australian MPs have banded together to launch a new centrist political party which they say is a response to an increasingly divisive landscape.

The Community Strong Australia party - launched in Canberra on Thursday - will offer "unity over division and reason over rage", will have no leader and will allow members to vote freely, rather than along party lines.

Its two members - Sydney MPs Zali Steggall and Allegra Spender - are from a group of independent MPs known as "teals" who share socially liberal values and want greater climate action.

The party will offer an "alternate political force" to the current two-party system in Australia, the pair said.

Australia's political landscape had traditionally been dominated by the two major parties - the centre-left Labor and the Liberal-Nationals Coalition, which leans conservative.

Labor won a landslide victory at last year's federal election, securing a second term in power, while the Coalition suffered its worst defeat ever, followed by months of in-fighting.

In recent months, right-wing party One Nation - led by Pauline Hanson -  has seen a surge in support, including one poll that found she was the preferred prime minister.

Asked if the recent rise in support for One Nation and its anti-immigration rhetoric had spurred their decision to form a new party, Steggall and Spender said they had been guided by what their voters were telling them.

"We absolutely hear those grievances," Spender said. "People are frustrated and tired of the status quo," she said, adding that "if I wasn't in politics, I wouldn't know who to vote for".

Spender, who won her seat in 2022, said the party wants to "hear from communities beyond our own that want a voice that genuinely reflects them".

Steggall, a former barrister and Winter Olympian, has been a federal MP since 2019, after she unseated the former prime minister Tony Abbott in an electorate that had been held by the Liberal Party for more than a century.

"We don't want the in-fighting, we don't want the blame game. We want solutions that will make a difference to us," Steggall said.

The new party "offers unity over division and reason over rage," she said, and was an "invitation" to voters "to come and build the kind of Australia we want".

[Lähde: The Guardian]
New party dubbed Community Strong Australia follows secret talks about future of community independents

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Teal independents Zali Steggall and Allegra Spender have launched a new political party called Community Strong Australia, with the stated aim of providing a centrist alternative for voters amid the rise of One Nation and turmoil inside the Coalition.

The party will focus on issues including housing affordability, cost of living, climate change, childcare, education, healthcare and social cohesion, according to Steggall, the member for Warringah.

She and Spender have distanced the new party from the Climate 200 movement and its major donors, including Scott Farquhar and Mike Cannon-Brooks, stating on Thursday they would not be involved.

The pair denied the move was a bid to skirt new political electoral laws – including spending and donation caps – which disadvantaged smaller players.

Community Strong Australia, which carries teal-coloured branding, would “support community-backed candidates” for election in both the House of Representatives and Senate, Steggall said when announcing the long-rumoured party.

“The community independent movement has shown what’s possible when people unite around shared values and practical solutions. Community Strong Australia is about extending that opportunity to more Australians,” she said.

Steggall and Spender unveiled the party on Thursday after weeks of speculation and secret talks about the future of the independents movement. Despite a wave of so-called teal MPs being elected to parliament in recent elections, at this stage only the Sydney MPs Steggall and Spender have declared their plan to join the party.

Fellow crossbencher Nicolette Boele said she was considering her options.

Steggall said the party would extend the “community independent” model to more Australians and more communities across the country.

“Australia is at a turning point, and people are worried about what the future holds. Community Strong Australia offers unity over division and reason over rage,” she said.

“At a time when others are promoting conflict and hate, I feel a strong sense of responsibility to provide a real political alternative and promote a positive narrative about what Australia is and what we can achieve together.”

payload.title: Australialaiset sitoutumattomat kansanedustajat perustivat uuden keskustapuolueen
payload.summary: Sydneyä edustavat sitoutumattomat kansanedustajat Zali Steggall ja Allegra Spender ovat perustaneet Australiassa uuden keskustalaisen puolueen nimeltä Community Strong Australia.
payload.content:
Sydneyä edustavat sitoutumattomat kansanedustajat Zali Steggall ja Allegra Spender ovat perustaneet Australiassa uuden keskustalaisen puolueen, jonka he sanovat tarjoavan vaihtoehdon maan kiristyneeseen poliittiseen ilmapiiriin, nykyiseen kaksipuolueasetelmaan ja äänestäjille, jotka etsivät heidän mukaansa järkeä vastakkainasettelun sijaan.

## Puolue lupaa vapaampaa äänestämistä

Community Strong Australia -niminen puolue lanseerattiin torstaina Canberrassa. Steggallin ja Spenderin mukaan puolueen viesti on tarjota kansalaisille ”yhtenäisyyttä jakautumisen sijaan” ja ”järkeä raivon sijaan”.

Puolueella ei lähteiden mukaan ole johtajaa, ja sen jäsenille luvataan mahdollisuus äänestää vapaasti sen sijaan, että he sitoutuisivat yhtenäiseen puoluelinjaan. Steggall ja Spender kuvaavat puoluetta vaihtoehtoiseksi poliittiseksi voimaksi Australian nykyiselle kaksipuoluejärjestelmälle.

Molemmat kansanedustajat kuuluvat niin sanottuihin teal-sitoutumattomiin. Ryhmään yhdistetään sosiaaliliberaaleja arvoja ja vahvempia ilmastotoimia ajavia riippumattomia edustajia. Steggall on Warringahin kansanedustaja, ja Spender kuuluu lähteiden mukaan Sydneyn alueen sitoutumattomiin kansanedustajiin.

## Taustalla paineita puoluekentässä

Uuden puolueen perustamista on kuvattu vastaukseksi yhä jakavampaan poliittiseen maisemaan. The Guardianin mukaan sen tavoitteeksi on asetettu keskustalaisen vaihtoehdon tarjoaminen äänestäjille tilanteessa, jossa One Nation on nousussa ja liberaali-kansallisen koalition sisällä on ollut kuohuntaa.

Steggallin mukaan puolue aikoo keskittyä muun muassa asumisen kohtuuhintaisuuteen, elinkustannuksiin, ilmastonmuutokseen, varhaiskasvatukseen, koulutukseen, terveydenhuoltoon ja sosiaaliseen yhteenkuuluvuuteen. Nämä painotukset kytkevät uuden puolueen sekä arjen kustannuksiin että laajempiin ilmasto- ja palvelukysymyksiin.

## Suhde Climate 200 -liikkeeseen rajataan

Steggall ja Spender ovat myös tehneet pesäeroa Climate 200 -liikkeeseen ja sen merkittäviin rahoittajiin. Heidän mukaansa liike sekä tunnetut tukijat Scott Farquhar ja Mike Cannon-Brooks eivät ole mukana uudessa puolueessa.

Puolueen perustamista edelsivät The Guardianin mukaan salaiset keskustelut yhteisöpohjaisten sitoutumattomien tulevaisuudesta. Uusi puolue pyrkii kokoamaan tämän asetelman ympärille järjestäytyneemmän poliittisen vaihtoehdon, mutta samalla se korostaa jäsenille luvattua vapautta äänestää asiakysymyksissä ilman pakollista puoluelinjaa.
summary_bullets: Zali Steggall ja Allegra Spender perustivat Community Strong Australia -puolueen Canberrassa.
Puolue sanoo tarjoavansa keskustalaisen vaihtoehdon Australian kaksipuoluejärjestelmälle.
Uusi puolue lupaa, ettei sillä ole johtajaa ja että jäsenet voivat äänestää vapaasti.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu paketin BBC- ja Guardian-aineistoihin. Mukaan on jätetty vain lähteissä mainitut tiedot; sekava BBC-koontilohkon muu uutisaineisto on rajattu pois.

Allegra Spender (left) and Zali Steggall say their new party will offer 'reason over rage' Two independent Australian MPs have banded together to launch a new centrist political party which they say is a response to an increasingly divisive landscape. The Community Strong Australia party - launched in Canberra on Thursday - will offer "unity over division and reason over rage", will have no leader and will allow members to vote freely, rather than along party lines. Its two members - Sydney MPs Zali Steggall and Allegra Spender - are from a group of independent MPs known as "teals" who share socially liberal values and want greater climate action. The party will offer an "alternate political force" to the current two-party system in Australia, the pair said.

The party will focus on issues including housing affordability, cost of living, climate change, childcare, education, healthcare and social cohesion, according to Steggall, the member for Warringah. She and Spender have distanced the new party from the Climate 200 movement and its major donors, including Scott Farquhar and Mike Cannon-Brooks, stating on Thursday they would not be involved.
